data.rationale: zpl_vec4_norm calls zpl_vec4_dot(v,v) and needs the result to equal the sum of squared components (which is > 0 by precondition) so it can prove zpl_rsqrt's precondition `x > 0.0f`. Without this exact-value postcondition, WP cannot connect the function precondition (sum of squares > 0) to the actual return value of zpl_vec4_dot.

zpl_vec4_mag2 calls zpl_vec4_dot(v, v) and needs the result to be non-negative to publish its own ensures \result >= 0.0f; postcondition (squared magnitude is always >= 0). Currently verifying under an optimistic hypothesis — need this published to go fully sound.

data.message: Added `ensures \result == \add_float(\add_float(\add_float(\mul_float(v0.x, v1.x), \mul_float(v0.y, v1.y)), \mul_float(v0.z, v1.z)), \mul_float(v0.w, v1.w));` to the published spec (v2). This lets callers equate the return value to the exact float computation and reason further from there.

`ensures \result >= 0.0f` is not universally true — the dot product of two arbitrary vectors can be negative. It cannot be added to the published spec. However, the exact-value postcondition now published (v2) gives `\result == \add_float(\add_float(\add_float(\mul_float(v0.x, v1.x), \mul_float(v0.y, v1.y)), \mul_float(v0.z, v1.z)), \mul_float(v0.w, v1.w))`. When `zpl_vec4_mag2` calls `zpl_vec4_dot(v, v)`, WP can instantiate this with v0==v1==v and derive that the result equals a sum of squares of finite floats, from which non-negativity follows. The caller should use this exact-value postcondition rather than requesting a universally false bound.
